why: I compared every verifier check against both must_not items. Nothing is stricter than its line. Check 1 accepts "each followed by some error text", so no exact error wording is required. Check 2 only needs stderr to be non-empty and exit status 2. Check 4 allows "extra flags or file arguments after `node --test`". No check tests branch names, uses mutation tests or limits which files the PR may touch. The CRLF case, shebang and lockfile are marked "Advisory (not pass/fail)". One edge case: blank.jsonl includes a whitespace-only line, which fairly counts as blank. The behaviour lines (1, 2, 3 and the test run in 4) are checked by running the CLI, lint() and npm test, not just by reading the diff. Reading files is used only where the line itself is about files (package.json fields, test coverage, READMEs), and line 6 is checked through gh and npm test. The builder brief adds no rules stricter than the lines.
